meta.title: Nephrology Literature Update
meta.query: Clinical nephrology — RCTs, systematic reviews & meta-analyses (humans, English)
meta.source: PubMed (NLM) abstracts; summaries and appraisals generated automatically from those abstracts. Each entry links to its PubMed record and DOI.
meta.note: Summaries and PICO are machine analyses of the source abstracts; criteria marked “not specified” were not stated. Read the source before acting clinically.
meta.appraisal_source: Automated critical appraisal (clinical bottom-line, relevance, caveat).

articles.authors: Tang W, Jiang W, Wang Z, Zhang C, Li T et al.
articles.title: Peritoneal catheter fixation versus nonfixation in open surgery: A meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 13 studies (1,275 patients) comparing peritoneal dialysis (PD) catheter fixation versus nonfixation during open surgical placement.

pico.population: Patients undergoing open surgery for peritoneal dialysis catheter placement.
pico.outcome: Catheter displacement, catheter malfunction, infection, bleeding, operating time.

inclusion: Studies comparing PD catheter fixation with nonfixation in open surgery.
Available in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, or Wanfang databases.

appraisal.bottom_line: Fixing the PD catheter during open surgery significantly reduces the risk of catheter displacement (OR 0.08, 95% CI 0.04-0.16; P < 0.00001) at the cost of a slightly longer operating time (mean difference 4.18 minutes, 95% CI 1.42-6.94; P = 0.003).
appraisal.relevance: Catheter migration is a common cause of PD failure; this study provides evidence that a simple surgical fixation step can mitigate this risk without increasing complications like infection or bleeding.
appraisal.caveat: The analysis is limited to open surgery; results may not generalize to laparoscopic or percutaneous placement techniques. Heterogeneity between studies was not explicitly detailed for all outcomes.

articles.authors: Wang H, Zhou W, Jiang Y
articles.title: Sustained potassium control and recurrent hyperkalemia during individualized potassium-guided sodium zirconium cyclosilicate titration in maintenance hemodialysis: a post hoc analysis of a randomized trial.
articles.summary: A post hoc analysis of a randomized trial evaluating the efficacy of individualized sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) titration for sustained potassium control in maintenance hemodialysis patients.

pico.population: 116 maintenance hemodialysis patients with chronic hyperkalemia.
pico.intervention: Individualized potassium-guided SZC therapy on non-dialysis days.
pico.outcome: Sustained response (at least 3 of 4 predialysis potassium values between 4.0-5.0 mmol/L during months 3-6).

inclusion: Participants in the original randomized trial.

appraisal.bottom_line: SZC treatment resulted in a significantly higher probability of sustained potassium control (43.1% vs 13.8%; aRR 3.02, 95% CI 1.49-6.14) and fewer recurrent hyperkalemic excursions (potassium ≥ 5.5 mmol/L; aRR 0.31, 95% CI 0.18-0.55).
appraisal.relevance: Managing the 'long-gap' interdialytic potassium rise is a major challenge in HD; SZC provides a pharmacological tool for more consistent control.
appraisal.caveat: This is a post hoc analysis of a single-center, open-label trial with a small sample size; clinical outcomes (e.g., mortality or cardiovascular events) were not assessed.

articles.authors: Chu D, Liu B, Soh KL, Saidi HI, Japar S
articles.title: Effectiveness of a self-management intervention on clinical outcomes among patients with type 2 diabetes at high risk for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: A randomized controlled trial evaluating a 12-week structured self-management intervention for type 2 diabetes (T2DM) patients at high risk for diabetic kidney disease (DKD).

pico.population: 134 patients with T2DM at high risk of DKD (based on a validated prediction model).
pico.intervention: 12-week structured self-management program followed by 12-week follow-up.
pico.outcome: HbA1c, eGFR, SBP, LDL-C, UACR, BMI, and waist circumference.

inclusion: Classified as high risk for DKD using a validated prediction model.

appraisal.bottom_line: A 12-week self-management program significantly improved HbA1c, eGFR, systolic blood pressure, and LDL-C compared to usual care, though no significant differences were found for UACR or BMI.
appraisal.relevance: Early intervention in high-risk diabetic patients may slow the progression to overt DKD by optimizing modifiable risk factors.
appraisal.caveat: The follow-up period was short (24 weeks), and the improvement in eGFR over such a brief interval should be interpreted cautiously as a surrogate for long-term renal protection. The study was conducted at a single tertiary hospital.

articles.title: A Review of Detection Probes for Vanin-1: Development and Biological Applications in Various Inflammatory Diseases.
articles.summary: A systematic review of the development and biological applications of detection probes for Vascular non-inflammatory molecule-1 (Vanin-1) in inflammatory diseases, including AKI.

pico.population: Patients or models of inflammatory diseases (AKI, IBD, liver injury, RA).
pico.outcome: Probe performance (sensitivity, specificity) and biological application.

inclusion: Studies on Vanin-1 probes developed in recent years.

appraisal.bottom_line: Vanin-1 is an emerging biomarker for early diagnosis of AKI and other inflammatory states; various highly sensitive probes are being developed to facilitate its clinical translation.
appraisal.relevance: Early detection of AKI remains a 'holy grail' in nephrology; Vanin-1 probes may offer a more specific diagnostic tool than current standards.
appraisal.caveat: This is a technical review of probe chemistry and early biological applications; it does not provide clinical diagnostic accuracy data (e.g., sensitivity/specificity in human cohorts).

articles.authors: Li SG, Yu R, Zhang Y, Zhang L, Zhang J et al.
articles.title: Complement-amplified thrombotic microangiopathy in systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis: a systematic review of 78 reported patients.
articles.summary: A systematic review of 78 patients with complement-amplified thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) occurring in the context of SLE and lupus nephritis.

pico.population: 78 patients with SLE/LN and associated TMA.

inclusion: Full-text sources or citable abstracts with extractable data.
exclusion: China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) sources (due to lack of verifiable search record).

appraisal.bottom_line: TMA in SLE/LN is highly heterogeneous; while 62.8% of patients showed renal improvement following various treatments (including complement inhibitors), the evidence is limited to case reports.
appraisal.relevance: Recognizing TMA in lupus nephritis is critical as it may require therapies beyond standard immunosuppression, such as complement blockade.
appraisal.caveat: The evidence is of very low certainty due to reliance on selectively published case reports and abstracts. The review also noted protocol deviations, including single-reviewer screening and extraction.

articles.authors: Liu M, Chen H, Liu Y, Xi Y, Su J et al.
articles.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the effects of non-pharmacological interventions in improving psychological status and sleep quality among hemodialysis patients.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (871 participants) evaluating non-pharmacological interventions for psychological status and sleep quality in hemodialysis patients.

appraisal.bottom_line: Non-pharmacological interventions significantly improved depression (SMD -0.62, 95% CI -0.87 to -0.37), anxiety (SMD -0.86, 95% CI -1.23 to -0.49), and sleep quality (SMD -0.94, 95% CI -1.33 to -0.55) in MHD patients.
appraisal.relevance: Psychological distress and poor sleep are highly prevalent in dialysis patients; these findings support the use of non-drug therapies to improve quality of life.
appraisal.caveat: There was high heterogeneity for anxiety (I2=79%) and sleep quality (I2=87%), and the certainty of evidence was low for these outcomes. Potential publication bias was noted for depression scores.

articles.authors: Navratil P, Princlova H, Izmaylov O, Tranova MN
articles.title: Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy in Kidney Transplant Recipients: an Updated Systematic Review and Surgical Perspective>.
articles.summary: A cross-sectional study of 135 kidney transplant recipients investigating the relationship between parathyroid hormone (PTH), vitamin D, and bone mineral density (BMD).

pico.population: 135 kidney transplant recipients (mean 71.4 months post-transplant) in Vietnam.
pico.outcome: Bone mineral density (T-score) at three skeletal sites.

inclusion: Underwent simultaneous measurement of PTH, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, and DXA.

appraisal.bottom_line: PTH levels above 65 pg/mL were inversely associated with BMD (T-score decrement of 0.37 per 100 pg/mL PTH increase; P < 0.001). The PTH-to-vitamin D ratio was a slightly better predictor of bone loss than PTH alone.
appraisal.relevance: Post-transplant bone disease is common (76.3% in this cohort); maintaining PTH within the KDIGO-recommended range may be vital for skeletal health.
appraisal.caveat: The title provided ('Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy...') completely contradicts the abstract content (PTH and BMD), suggesting a metadata error. The study is cross-sectional and cannot establish a causal link between PTH and bone loss.
